newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Five bids submitted for Hungary K&H bank sale.
newsitem.headline: Five bids submitted for Hungary K&H bank sale.

text.p: Five investors have submitted bids for the privatisation of Kereskedelmi Bank (K&H), one of Hungary's largest commercial banks, the state privatisation agency APV told Reuters on Monday.

"We have received five bids," said APV managing director Gabor Nemeth. "APV's board of director will make a proposal to the Finance Minister on April 23 as to which investors should qualify for the second round of the tender."
Nemeth declined to disclose further details.
Earlier press reports said the potential bidders included Holland's ING Bank, Belgium's Kredietbank and Austria's Creditanstalt.

Hungary plans to sell a stake of at least 25 percent plus one vote in K&H to a strategic investor, who will have the right to invite a financial investor to raise the bank's equity at a later date by a minimum $30 million.

K&H said recently it had come to a preliminary agreement with the European Bank of Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) on such an a capital increase but this was subject to the approval of the new strategic investor.

K&H increased its balance sheet total to 360 billion forints in 1996 from 326.8 billion in 1995, while after-tax profits grew to 2.7 billion forints last year from 1.9 billion forints in 1995, K&H said.
